conservation_status.value: endangered (FAO, 2007); about 250 birds kept by a dozen breeders in Japan

value: exceptionally long non-moulting tail, over 1.5 m and reported up to 12 m
tail feathers grow about 0.7-1.3 m per year
designated a Special Natural Treasure of Japan in 1952, the only chicken breed with that status
kept in special elevated hutches to protect the tail
ancestor of the German Phoenix breed

history_summary.value: The Onagadori was bred in the 1600s in what is now Kochi Prefecture from other long-tailed Japanese breeds, prized purely for its extraordinary, continuously growing tail. It was named a Special Natural Treasure of Japan in 1952 and is now endangered, kept by only a small number of dedicated breeders.
